# kener_maintenance (Resource)

Manages a Kener scheduled-maintenance window. The schedule is an iCalendar RRULE plus a duration; individual occurrences (events) are generated by Kener and are not managed here.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "kener_monitor" "api" {
  tag          = "my-api"
  name         = "My API"
  monitor_type = "API"
  type_data    = jsonencode({ url = "https://api.example.com/health" })
}

resource "kener_maintenance" "weekly" {
  title            = "Weekly database maintenance"
  description      = "Routine Sunday maintenance window"
  start_date_time  = 1735732800 # Unix timestamp (seconds), minute-aligned
  rrule            = "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU"
  duration_seconds = 3600 # 1 hour
  status           = "ACTIVE"

  monitors = [
    {
      monitor_tag = kener_monitor.api.tag
      impact      = "MAINTENANCE"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `duration_seconds` (Number) Duration of each maintenance occurrence, in seconds (at least 1).
- `rrule` (String) Recurrence rule in iCalendar RRULE format, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU`.
- `start_date_time` (Number) Start time as a Unix timestamp (seconds). Kener aligns this to the minute.
- `title` (String) Maintenance title.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description.
- `monitors` (Attributes List) Monitors affected by this maintenance, with their impact. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--monitors))
- `status` (String) Whether the maintenance is enabled. One of `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`. Defaults to `ACTIVE`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Numeric identifier assigned by Kener.
- `url` (String) Absolute public URL of the maintenance.

<a id="nestedatt--monitors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `monitors`

Required:

- `monitor_tag` (String) Tag of the affected monitor.

Optional:

- `impact` (String) Impact on the monitor. One of `UP`, `DOWN`, `DEGRADED`, `MAINTENANCE`. Defaults to `MAINTENANCE`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Maintenance windows are imported by their numeric id.
terraform import kener_maintenance.weekly 5
```
